lint_missed: In side views the hazard band breaks into three unrelated pieces: the slashed orange front fender, the sill band and the rear-quarter panel. Each piece ends at a wheel arch instead of wrapping across it, and the diagonals on the rear-quarter panel change angle at the rear arch.

The orange-to-black change on the front fender is a ragged, torn edge just ahead of the door shut line (beltline crop). At speed it reads as a smudge rather than a deliberate cut, and it does not clearly cross or clearly avoid the shut line.
The bonnet 451 is white on orange and sits right against the black bonnet mask. It has much lower contrast than the door number (white on a red box) and the rear number (white on black).

Signal red shows up in several places: the full-width front splitter, the door number box and slivers by the tail lights and rear haunch. It reads as scattered trim rather than the one alert panel the brief asks for.
fixes: The car reads as two different designs. The nose, bonnet and front fenders are solid orange with a black chevron mask, while the doors, roof, rear quarters and tail are near-black. From the front it is an orange car; from the side and from the chase camera it is a black one. Only the roof chevron spine links the two.

The hazard tape does not run nose to tail. The low band starts at the front door edge and stops at the rear wheel arch. Behind the arch it is replaced by a separate tall panel of diagonals at a different angle. It never reaches the nose, and the chase view has no tape at all: the rear bumper, the diffuser surround and the tail are plain black apart from the engine-cover chevrons.

The car is still well short of the density in the Unit-01 reference. Large plain black areas remain: the upper door and the roof side above EMERGENCY, the rear quarter above the band, and the whole rear face. The tactical text is a single cluster next to the door number, so a close look finds nothing new anywhere else on the car.

lint_missed: The red block behind the bonnet 451 is offset from the number in 3D, so part of the number sits on black, not on the red panel (front view and nose crop).
Where the fender diagonals fold over the fender crown and down the bumper sides, they turn into a zigzag/moire pattern (front view, both fenders).
The rear-deck diagonals bend into arcs over the rear haunches in the chase view instead of staying straight tape.
On side_r the MAGI SYSTEM text is clipped at the rear intake ('AGI SYSTEM'). On side_l an orange slash crowds the end of '2/3 APPROVE'.
fixes: The upper half of the car is still plain black slab: the door above the sill tape, the flanks either side of the bonnet chevrons, the roof sides and the rear quarter above the window. Front and front34 are mostly empty black. The car is busier than the concept, but it is still clearly plainer than the EVA RT Type-01 reference he pointed to. There are almost no layered angular panels, only stripes plus one text block per side, so the 'denser, on every view' request is only half met.

The front fender hazard stripes stop reading as tape. Over the fender crown and around the front arch they bend into fanned slashes and fine zigzags, which are noisy in the front view. They also lean at a different angle from the straight sill band on the door, so the nose and the side read as two stripe treatments.

On the nose the red alert block sits low and right of the 451: the '4' and the tops of the digits hang off its left and top edge onto black. On the right rear quarter the 'MAGI SYSTEM / 2/3 APPROVE' lines are cut off at the start by the intake and the orange slashes, and on the left they run into a slash.

lint_missed: Nose crop: below the second bonnet chevron, the orange shapes break into clipped fragments around the badge and the bonnet crease. They read as a chevron cut by the panel, not as deliberate pieces.

Side shots: the hex field starts with a hard edge at the front of the door and A-pillar, and the front fender in front of it is black apart from the low hazard stripes. In 3D this looks like a panel boundary, not a design edge.
fixes: The hex field from the door to the tail and over the roof is an even, directionless scatter of hexes that are all the same size. Nothing larger sits underneath it, so in the 200 px side and squint shots the car reads as busy orange-on-black texture rather than one idea. It needs one big raked shape or density gradient, the way the EVA RT reference's pieces all lean the same way.

The front third is still the plain car. The bonnet carries only two chevrons over a large black field, and the upper front fenders above the arches are bare black. The only hexes on the nose are a small cluster in the bonnet's top-right corner, and nothing balances them on the left beside the 451 panel. From the front and front34 shots the nose looks like a different, emptier design than the doors.

Three motifs don't connect: hexes on the sides and roof, raked hazard diagonals on the sills and bumper, and forward chevrons on the bonnet, roof spine and engine cover. Red also appears four times (accent hexes, number panels, the EMERGENCY bar, a large red rear bumper) where the brief asks for once. The roof and engine-cover chevrons stop where the side hexes start, so the top and sides read as separate panels.

The 50 m idea doesn't read. In side_l-200 and side_r-200 the car is an even orange-and-black pattern from nose to tail, with a red-and-white blob on the door. The nose is not 'mostly orange': in front.png it is about half orange, with large black shards and two big red blocks on the bonnet. In chase.png the engine cover and rear deck are as bright orange (chevrons and diagonal bars) as the nose, so nothing burns down to a black tail. The orange needs to dominate the front third and clearly die away toward a mostly black rear third, so the change reads in the 200 px side and chase shots.

The motifs don't form one system, and the hexes have no direction. The bonnet has big angular tiger-stripe shards (front.png, crop-nose.png), the engine cover has chevrons and diagonal bars (chase.png), the sills have hazard tape, and the sides have hex cells. The four don't connect. The hex cells come in loose clusters on the door top, the roof edge and the haunch (side_l.png, crop-beltline.png). They don't flow along the rake or lean the same way as the hazard diagonals, so they read as scattered confetti rather than a display that bursts from the nose. Turn the nose shards into hex fragments of the same system, and make the clusters stream rearward and thin out along the rake.

The type block on the door is a cluster of stickers. MAGI, BLOOD TYPE: BLUE and 601 are three white rounded pills stacked around the red 451 block, and they crowd the number (crop-beltline.png, side_l.png). Set them inside the cell or tape fields as one secondary group, away from the number box. There is also a green bar beside the '88' digit readout on the left haunch (crop-beltline.png), and a green '0' shows in front34.png. Green breaks the brief's black, orange, red and white palette, so make those marks white or orange.
lint_missed: The EMERGENCY text on the red roof panel reads upside down from the front in front.png and front34.png, and no rear camera shows it.
The window opening cuts the hex cells at the top of the door and the roof edge part-way through a cell (crop-beltline.png), so their edges neither clearly cross nor clearly avoid the window line.

answers.note: The front third is now a solid orange field: bonnet, front fenders and nose sides. Its rear edge is stepped along hex sides and breaks into cells over the door. The cells cool along the rake from orange through burnt orange to charcoal, so the rear third is black with charcoal cells. The hazard tape and the chevron lane cool the same way: orange to about u 0.40 (0.59 on top), then burnt orange, then charcoal. The engine-cover chevrons, the tail chevrons and the rear corners are now charcoal and burnt orange. The red twin panel on the bonnet is gone, and 451 sits in a black field cut out of the orange. Checked in the flat views only, not in the sim.

The nose is no longer cells chopped by the bonnet's map. It is the honeycomb fused solid, with a hex-stepped edge where it breaks up. Behind it there is one system: large, medium and small cells, chosen by their position along the 45 degree rake (the hazard tape's lean). As they cool they survive only in raked streams that narrow towards the tail. Each smaller size fills the gaps the larger ones left. Cells the paint can't show whole (at the window line, the arches or the edge of the view) are left out, so none is cut part-way.

The white pills (MAGI, BLOOD TYPE: BLUE, 601) are gone. The secondary type is now black plates in the sill tape with orange hairline frames and orange labels, away from the number: TOKYO-3 ahead of the side intake and BLOOD TYPE / BLUE behind it. MAGI moved into the rear corner window with LCL. Green readout and green 0: skipped, sim decal. The design draws no green; the readout is the sim's door light panel, which the cells keep clear of.

fixes: The hexagon display still doesn't burst out of the nose. The fix was answered done ('honeycomb fused solid with a hex-stepped edge'), but in front.png, front34.png and crop-nose.png the bonnet and front fenders show no hex at all. They carry big black tiger-stripe shards, diagonal hazard bars and a black double chevron. The first cells appear only behind the front wheel, on the door and the roof rail (side_l.png). From the front and front34 the car reads as 'orange with tiger stripes', and the hex idea starts mid-car as a second motif. The orange-to-black burn along the rake now reads well in side_l-200 and chase-200. What's left is to make the nose speak the same language: the bonnet shards and the rear edge of the orange field should be visibly made of cells, large ones, so they show from the front camera.

The mid and rear cells have no visible second layer. In side_l.png and front34.png the orange cells on the door top and roof rail render as small round dots in loose clusters, like polka dots, not three sizes streaming rearward. The charcoal cells meant to fill the black tail barely show in the side shots: the rear haunch and rear bumper side in side_l.png read as bare black around the UMBILICAL CABLE plate. They show only on the rear face in chase.png. Make the large and medium cells clearly bigger than the small ones where they meet the orange. Make the charcoal cells a step lighter so the black third holds a visible texture from the side cameras, not only from behind.

The door type stack crowds the number. The red EMERGENCY bar sits directly on top of the red block behind 451, so in side_l.png, side_r.png and both side 200 px shots the two merge into one red T-shaped blob, and EMERGENCY stops reading as separate from the number zone. Separate them with a clear black gap of about a cell's height, or move EMERGENCY up along the door top, so the number keeps its own field.
lint_missed: The TOKYO-3 sill plate just behind the front wheel reads as 'YO-3' in side_l.png and crop-beltline.png: the front wheel arch/shut line cuts off its first letters.

The large diagonal hazard bars on the front fender stop at the fender's rear shut line (crop-beltline.png, side_l.png). The door starts with orange field and hex cells instead, so at that shut line the pattern changes rather than clearly crossing it.

answers.note: The nose is now large cells (radius 0.04 u, up from 0.026) with black gaps, every one painted whole, so the bonnet and the field's rear edge are visibly hexes. In the 21:44 top and front34 shots the bonnet reads as a honeycomb. The whole-island fender paints and the pulled-back edges that made the black shards are gone, and 451 sits in a gap left by its cells. Not fully fixed: on the curved front fenders the cells still distort into irregular orange pieces in front34. The new camera set has no straight front shot.

Cell sizes are now 0.04 / 0.024 / 0.012 u, so large and medium are clearly bigger than small, and the gaps scale with the cell. Charcoal went from #454545 to #5c5c5c, and the cooling cells keep more of the rake streams (fewer holes, wider streams). The rear haunch and quarter show grey hex texture in both side shots and in rear34. Cells now avoid the plates and type whole instead of being cut part-way. The mid-door is still on the sparse side.

The red block behind 451 is gone. The number sits on black between two red uprights rising from the pinline, which opens under it. EMERGENCY moved up and shrank slightly (cells r 0.02), leaving a black gap above the uprights' tops; in the 21:44 side shots the two no longer form a red T. The gap is about half a cell, not a full cell: the door top (v 0.83 at the front of the row) doesn't leave room for more.

fixes: The nose has been the first fix for three rounds now. It has improved, but from the front it still doesn't read as hexes. In top.png the bonnet is now clearly large hex cells, so that part of last round's 'done' holds. In front34.png and crop-nose.png the front fenders, nose corners and bumper read as tiger stripes: full-height orange and black diagonal hazard bars, plus warped orange shards and black chevrons over the headlights. In side_l, side_r and both side 200 px shots the whole front fender, from the nose back to the shut line behind the wheel, is the same big diagonal bars, and the hexes only start on the door. So from front34 and the sides the nose speaks a second language, and the idea of 'a hex display bursting out of the nose' is only true from directly above. The front fender and nose corners should be orange carrying the large cells, with the hazard bars kept to the low tape. If the front still reads as stripes next round, the concept has hit its ceiling.

The door type is still not on one system, which was his 'alignment/spacing' complaint. In side_l.png and side_r.png the three text elements sit at three heights and share no edge or baseline. EMERGENCY starts at the door front. The BLOOD TYPE: BLUE plate floats under the right half of EMERGENCY, roughly under the G, lined up with nothing. UMBILICAL CABLE starts where EMERGENCY ends, a step higher, on the haunch shoulder (crop-beltline.png). Each plate is sized well around its own text, but as a group they look scattered. Give the secondary plates a shared left edge or a single raked line, and tie them to EMERGENCY or the 451 brackets.

There are too many EMERGENCY marks, and the roof ones break the plate rule. In top.png the roof and engine cover carry two identical upright red EMERGENCY plates that don't lean 45°, plus the two door rows, so the word appears four times and is the loudest thing from above (top-200.png: two red blobs either side of the chevron lane). Keep one roof plate, or give the second a different job, and lean it like the side plates.
lint_missed: The large diagonal hazard bars on the front fender still stop at the fender's rear shut line behind the front wheel (side_l.png, side_r.png, front34.png), and the door starts with black field and hex cells. At that shut line the pattern changes instead of clearly crossing it.

On the curved front fenders and nose corners the hex cells distort into irregular orange shards (front34.png, crop-nose.png), so they don't read as cells from the low front camera. They do read in top.png.
In crop-beltline.png, at the far left, an orange cell at the A-pillar/door edge is cut part-way by the panel edge.

answers.note: skipped: concept question for Nickolaj. The front fender and nose corners still carry the hazard bars; the main session is putting the nose question to him.

The door's secondary type is now one plate holding two lines (BLOOD TYPE: BLUE over UMBILICAL CABLE), sharing one raked left edge and one line gap. It starts one pad behind the number's right red upright and is centred between the pinline and the EMERGENCY row. The separate haunch plate is gone, so the type on each door is three tied pieces: EMERGENCY, the number with its brackets, and the plate. Seen in the 22:01 side_l and side_r shots.

The rear-deck EMERGENCY plate is gone, so the word appears three times: both doors and the roof. The roof plate's ends are now raked at 45 degrees like the side plates, and it is as long as its text plus the same padding as above and below the letters. Seen in the 22:01 top and front34 shots.
